Lotto NZ

A jackpot year, not a growth year. FY26 gross sales rose ~3% to NZ$1.67bn (~$0.95bn) on the record NZ$55m (~$31m) Must Be Won Powerball draw of November 2025 and three NZ$20m+ (~$11m+) jackpots, beating the original NZ$1,575.7m (~$898m) budget by ~6% but landing roughly NZ$15–25m (~$9–14m) short of management's own June-2026 forecast of NZ$1,693.2m (~$965m). Profit before distribution (company forecast NZ$401.4m / ~$229m; audited figure unverified) is flat-to-down on FY25's NZ$405.1m (~$231m) because prize cost, a 71% step-up in the problem-gambling levy, tripled ticket costs and halved interest income absorbed the volume — margin on sales down ~120bps to ~23.7%. FY27 hinges on the Powerball matrix change (10→14 balls) and the arrival of up to 15 licensed online casinos.

Codere Group

A profitability quarter, not a growth quarter: group gross win rose just 6% to €344m (~$380m) but adj. EBITDA jumped 39% to €65.4m (~$72m), lifting margin ~450bps to 19.0%, with Retail (+32% to €54.0m on Mexico cost actions, Argentina and Spain) and Online (group-basis €11.3m vs €6.2m) both contributing and LTM retail EBITDA rising for an eighth straight quarter to €210.7m (~$233m). Public disclosure remains thin — no P&L below EBITDA, no net debt, no country split — and the €11.3m "online" EBITDA the group books is 2.7x the €4.2m Codere Online reports standalone, a definitional gap any buyer in the reported ~€2bn (~$2.2bn) sale process will price.

Angler Gaming

A clean, margin-rich quarter — revenue +10.0% to €8.72m (~$9.63m), EBIT +79.6% to €3.04m (~$3.36m) at a 34.9% margin, net profit more than doubled — that the market ignored because the same release announced a second re-cut of the B2B platform deal from 1 Nov 2026: lower fees, affiliate/royalty costs pushed to partners, and a €5.25m (~$5.8m) one-off "incentive" to be settled by forgiving partner receivables in exchange for five-year contracts.
